# rustnum

> rustnum is a NumPy-style n-dimensional array library for pure Rust. One type, `Array<T>`, covers 0-d, 1-d and n-d data. Function names, argument order and panic messages follow NumPy. Write `use rustnum as np;` and call `np::zeros`, `np::linalg::solve`, `np::random::Rng`, `np::fft::fft`, `np::poly::polyval`, `np::io::save_npy`. Element types: f32 f64 i32 i64 u8 usize bool Complex<f32> Complex<f64> f16 bf16. Views are copy-on-write, not write-through. Misuse (bad shape, index, axis) panics with NumPy's message; bad data (files, singular matrix) returns `np::Result`. Full NumPy table: docs/NUMPY_MAPPING.md. Contract: docs/API.md.

## Rules for writing rustnum code
- Always `use rustnum as np;`. `shape` is `&[usize]`, `axis` is `isize` (negative allowed).
- No keyword arguments. `a.sum(axis=1)` becomes `a.sum_axis(1)`. No keepdims: use `.expand_dims(axis)`.
- Float literals need `.0`: `np::arange(0.0, 5.0, 1.0)`. `np::array![1, 2]` is `Array<i32>`.
- Borrow to keep arrays: `&a + &b`. `a + b` moves both.
- Scalars work on either side: `&a * 2.0`, `1.0 - &a`. The scalar type must equal the element type.
- Math is mostly a method: `a.exp()`, not `np::exp(&a)`. Binary math functions are free functions: `np::maximum`, `minimum`, `power`, `arctan2`, `hypot`, `where_`, `logaddexp`, `fmod`, `remainder`, `floor_divide`, `divmod`, `copysign`, `heaviside`, `nextafter`, `ldexp`, `float_power`, `gcd`, `lcm`.
- `where` is `where_`. `-1` in reshape needs `reshape_infer(&[-1, 3])`.
- Comparisons are methods returning `Array<bool>`: `a.gt(0.5)`, `a.eq_elem(&b)`. `a == b` returns one bool.
- Fallible calls need `?`: `np::linalg::solve`, `inv`, `cholesky`, `lstsq`, `matrix_power`, `eig`, `eigvals`, all `np::io` functions (`load_npy`, `save_npy`, `load_csv`, `save_csv`, `savez`, `savez_compressed`, `load_npz`, `NpzFile::open`).
- Random methods need `let mut rng = np::random::Rng::seed(42);`. Streams differ from NumPy.
- A slice is a view, but a write never changes the parent. Use `a.slice_assign(..)` to write into part of an array.
- Complex arrays are `Array<np::Complex<f64>>` (complex128) and `Array<np::Complex<f32>>` (complex64); build with `np::Complex::new(re, im)`. `np::fft` takes real or complex arrays and returns complex arrays. `np::poly::roots` and `np::linalg::eig` still return `(re, im)` pairs. Real modulus is `np::absolute(&z)`; `z.abs()` returns a complex array.

## 10 NumPy to rustnum translations
```
np.arange(0, 6).reshape(2, 3)        np::arange(0.0, 6.0, 1.0).reshape(&[2, 3])
np.zeros((2, 3))                     np::zeros::<f64>(&[2, 3])
a + b                                &a + &b
a[:, 1]                              a.slice(&np::s![.., 1])
a[::2, 1:]                           a.slice(&np::s![..;2, 1..])
a.sum(axis=0)                        a.sum_axis(0)
a @ b                                a.matmul(&b)
np.linalg.solve(A, y)                np::linalg::solve(&a, &y)?
np.where(a > 0, a, 0.0)              np::where_(&a.gt(0.0), &a, 0.0)
rng = np.random.default_rng(42)      let mut rng = np::random::Rng::seed(42);
```

## Types and traits
- `Array<T>` — the array. Cheap to clone (shared buffer). Implements Clone Debug Display PartialEq Default Send Sync.
- `Element` — all element types. `Num: Element` — f32 f64 i32 i64 u8 usize. `Float: Num` — f32 f64.
- `IntoArray<T>` — anything array-like: `T`, `Array<T>`, `&Array<T>`, `Vec<T>`, `&[T]`, `[T; N]`.
- `np::Error` — variants include Singular, NotPositiveDefinite, Shape(String), DType, Parse, Format, NoConvergence, Io. `np::Result<T>`.
- `np::Complex<F>` — complex number `re + im*j`; an `Element` + `Num` (complex64 for f32, complex128 for f64).

## Construction
- `np::array![1.0, 2.0]`, `np::array![[1.0, 2.0], [3.0, 4.0]]` — array literal (ragged panics)
- `Array::from_vec(data, &[2, 3])` — from Vec and shape
- `Array::from_shape_fn(&[2, 3], |idx| value)` — np.fromfunction
- `Array::scalar(v)` — 0-d array
- `Array::from(vec)`, `iter.collect::<Array<T>>()` — 1-d
- `np::zeros::<T>(shape)`, `np::ones::<T>(shape)` — filled arrays
- `np::full(shape, v)` — constant
- `np::zeros_like(&a)`, `np::ones_like(&a)`, `np::full_like(&a, v)`
- `np::arange(start, stop, step)` — all three required, same type
- `np::linspace(start, stop, num)` — floats, endpoint included
- `np::logspace(start, stop, num)` — base 10
- `np::eye::<T>(n)`, `np::identity::<T>(n)`
- `np::diag(&v)` — 1-d to matrix, matrix to 1-d
- `np::tri::<T>(n)`, `np::tril(&a)`, `np::triu(&a)`
- `np::meshgrid(&x, &y)` — (X, Y), indexing xy

## Attributes and access
- `a.shape()` — &[usize]
- `a.ndim()`, `a.size()`, `a.len()` (axis 0, panics on 0-d), `a.is_empty()`
- `a.strides()` — in elements. `a.dtype()` — "float64" etc.
- `a.is_contiguous()`
- `a[[i, j]]`, `a[[i, j]] = v` — index with an array of usize
- `a.get(&[i, j])` — value. `a.set(&[i, j], v)`
- `a.item()` — the only value (size must be 1)
- `a.to_vec()` — Vec<T> in C order. `a.as_slice()` — Option<&[T]>, Some if contiguous
- `a.iter()` — elements in C order. `for x in &a` also works
- `a.to_contiguous()`, `a.copy()` (deep copy)
- `a.astype::<U>()` — cast, truncates like NumPy
- `a.map(|x| ..)` — new array. `a.mapv_inplace(|x| ..)`. `a.zip_map(&b, |x, y| ..)` — broadcasts
- `a.fill(v)`

## Indexing and slicing
- `np::s![1..3, .., -1]` — slice spec. Forms: `a..b` `a..` `..b` `..` `a..=b`, one index drops the axis, `;step`, `np::NEW_AXIS`
- `a.slice(&np::s![..;2, 1..;-1])` — O(1) view
- `a.slice_assign(&np::s![0, ..], v)` — write into a region, v is array-like and broadcasts
- `a.index_axis(axis, i)`, `a.row(i)`, `a.col(j)` — drop an axis (row, col are 2-d only)
- `a.mask(&m)` — a[m], 1-d result, m: Array<bool> with a's shape
- `a.mask_assign(&m, v)` — a[m] = v
- `a.take(&[0, 2], axis)` — np.take with usize indices
- `a.compress(&mask, axis)` — np.compress with 1-d bool mask
- `np::nonzero(&a)` — Vec<Array<usize>>. `np::argwhere(&a)`
- `np::searchsorted(&sorted, v)` — usize

## Operators
- `+ - * / %` — all borrow combinations, plus scalar on either side. Broadcast.
- `-a` — signed and float types. `+= -= *= /= %=` — right side Array, &Array or scalar
- `a.eq_elem(b)`, `a.ne_elem(b)`, `a.lt(b)`, `a.le(b)`, `a.gt(b)`, `a.ge(b)` — Array<bool>, b array-like
- `& | ^ !` on `Array<bool>`. `np::logical_and(&m1, &m2)`, `logical_or`, `logical_xor`, `logical_not(&m)`
- `a.allclose(&b, rtol, atol)` — bool, floats. `np::isclose(&a, &b, rtol, atol)` — Array<bool>
- `a.array_equal(&b)`
- `a.broadcast_to(&[3, 4])` — view. `np::broadcast_arrays(&a, &b)`. `np::broadcast_shapes(&s1, &s2)` — Option<Vec<usize>>

## Element-wise math (methods on float arrays unless noted)
- `exp exp2 expm1 log log2 log10 log1p sqrt cbrt square reciprocal` — log is natural log
- `sin cos tan arcsin arccos arctan sinh cosh tanh`
- `floor ceil round trunc abs sign` — abs, sign, square, clip also work on integers
- `a.round_decimals(n)` — round to `n` decimal places
- `a.powf(p)` — float exponent. `a.powi(n)` — integer exponent
- `a.clip(lo, hi)` — method only
- `a.is_nan()`, `a.is_inf()`, `a.is_finite()` — Array<bool>
- `a.sinc()`, `a.i0()`, `a.deg2rad()`, `a.rad2deg()`, `a.rint()`, `a.fix()`, `a.fabs()`, `a.positive()`, `a.negative()`
- `a.signbit()` — Array<bool>. `a.spacing()` — distance to next float
- `a.modf()` — (frac, int). `a.frexp()` — (mantissa, exponent: Array<i32>)
- `a.nan_to_num()`, `a.nan_to_num_with(nan, posinf, neginf)`
- `a.unwrap()`, `a.unwrap_with(discont, axis, period)`
- `a.sigmoid()`, `a.relu()` — extras, not NumPy
- Free functions:
  - `np::maximum(&a, &b)`, `np::minimum(&a, &b)` — broadcast, NaN propagates. Scalars allowed.
  - `np::power(&a, &b)`, `np::arctan2(&y, &x)`, `np::hypot(&a, &b)`
  - `np::where_(&cond, x, y)` — np.where(cond, x, y), x and y array-like
  - `np::logaddexp(&a, &b)`, `np::logaddexp2(&a, &b)`
  - `np::fmod(&a, &b)`, `np::remainder(&a, &b)`, `np::floor_divide(&a, &b)`, `np::divmod(&a, &b)` (returns (div, rem))
  - `np::copysign(&a, &b)`, `np::heaviside(&x, h0)`, `np::nextafter(&a, &b)`, `np::ldexp(&a, &e)`
  - `np::float_power(&a, &b)` — returns Array<f64>
  - `np::gcd(&a, &b)`, `np::lcm(&a, &b)` — i64
  - `np::ediff1d(&a)`, `np::ediff1d_with(&a, to_end, to_begin)`
  - `np::angle(&a)`, `np::angle_deg(&a)`
  - Windows: `np::hanning(m)`, `np::hamming(m)`, `np::blackman(m)`, `np::bartlett(m)`, `np::kaiser(m, beta)`

## Reductions (whole array returns a value; `_axis(axis)` removes that axis)
- `sum prod min max` — T. `sum_axis prod_axis min_axis max_axis`
- `mean var std` — floats only. `mean_axis var_axis std_axis`
- `var_ddof(ddof)`, `std_ddof(ddof)` — whole array. `var_ddof_axis(axis, ddof)`, `std_ddof_axis(axis, ddof)` — along axis
- `argmin argmax` — usize, flat index. `argmin_axis argmax_axis` — Array<usize>
- `any all` — bool. `any_axis all_axis`
- `cumsum cumprod` — flat 1-d. `cumsum_axis cumprod_axis` — keep shape
- `count_nonzero ptp` — whole array
- `median`, `median_axis(axis)`, `percentile(q)` — floats, q in 0..=100
- `nansum nanmean nanmax nanmin` — floats, whole array. `nansum_axis nanmean_axis nanmin_axis nanmax_axis`
- Empty min/max/argmin/argmax panic.
- Keep dims: `a.sum_axis(1).expand_dims(1)`

## Shape manipulation
- `a.reshape(&[2, 3])` — usize. `a.reshape_infer(&[-1, 3])` — isize, one -1 allowed
- `a.ravel()`, `a.flatten()`
- `a.t()` — reverse axes (view). `a.transpose(&[1, 0, 2])`, `permute_axes` (same)
- `a.swapaxes(a0, a1)`, `a.moveaxis(src, dst)`
- `a.squeeze()`, `a.squeeze_axis(axis)`, `a.expand_dims(axis)`
- `a.flip(axis)`, `a.flip_all()`, `a.roll(shift, axis)`
- `a.repeat(n, axis)`, `a.tile(&[2, 3])`
- `a.sort()` (last axis, NaN last), `a.sort_axis(axis)`, `a.argsort()`, `a.argsort_axis(axis)` — argsort gives Array<usize>
- `np::concatenate(&[&a, &b], axis)`, `np::stack(&[&a, &b], axis)`, `np::vstack(&[&a, &b])`, `np::hstack(&[&a, &b])`
- `np::split(&a, sections, axis)`, `np::array_split(&a, sections, axis)` — Vec<Array<T>>
- `np::unique(&a)` — sorted 1-d. `np::unique_counts(&a)` — (values, counts)
- `np::pad(&a, width, value)` — constant padding

## Linear algebra (np::linalg)
- `a.matmul(&b)` — 1-d, 2-d, batched n-d. f32/f64 use matrixmultiply.
- `a.dot(&b)`, `a.trace()`
- `np::linalg::outer(&a, &b)`, `np::linalg::inner(&a, &b)`, `np::linalg::vdot(&a, &b)`
- `np::linalg::det(&a)` — F. `slogdet(&a)` — (sign, logabsdet)
- `np::linalg::inv(&a)?`, `solve(&a, &b)?`, `lstsq(&a, &b)?` — Result<Array<F>>. Error::Singular if singular
- `np::linalg::pinv(&a)`
- `np::linalg::norm(&a)` — F. `norm_axis(&a, ord, axis)`, `vector_norm(&x, ord)`, `matrix_norm(&a, ord)`
- `np::linalg::cond(&a)` — 2-norm. `cond_ord(&a, ord)`
- `np::linalg::cholesky(&a)?` — lower triangle. Error::NotPositiveDefinite
- `np::linalg::qr(&a)` — (q, r), reduced
- `np::linalg::eigh(&a)` — (values ascending, vectors as columns), symmetric input. `eigvalsh(&a)` — values only
- `np::linalg::eig(&a)?` — Result<(w_re, w_im, v_re, v_im)>. `eigvals(&a)?` — Result<(re, im)>
- `np::linalg::svd(&a)` — (u, s descending, vt), reduced
- `np::linalg::matrix_rank(&a)` — usize. `matrix_power(&a, n)?` — Result<Array<F>>
- `np::linalg::multi_dot(&[&a, &b, &c])`
- `np::linalg::tensordot(&a, &b, &axes_a, &axes_b)`, `tensordot_n(&a, &b, n)`

## Complex arrays (Array<np::Complex<F>>)
- Operators broadcast and mix real and complex: `&z * &w`, `&z + &r` (r real array), `&z * 2.0`, `np::Complex::new(0.0, 1.0) * &z`
- `z.real()`, `z.imag()`, `z.conj()`, `z.angle()`, `z.angle_deg()`, `np::absolute(&z)` (real output)
- `z.exp()`, `log()`, `log2()`, `log10()`, `sqrt()`, `sin()`, `cos()`, `tan()`, `sinh()`, `cosh()`, `tanh()`, `np::power(&z, &w)`
- `z.is_nan()`, `is_inf()`, `is_finite()`; `z.sum()`, `prod()`, `mean()`, `mean_axis(k)`, `sum_axis(k)`, `cumsum()`
- `a.matmul(&b)`, `a.dot(&b)`, `a.vdot(&b)` (conjugates `a`); `z.sort()`, `max()`, `min()` are lexicographic
- `a.astype::<np::Complex<f64>>()` from real gives `x + 0j`; `.npy`/`.npz` store `<c8`/`<c16`
- Display `[1.+2.j 3.-4.j]`

## float16 / bfloat16 (np::f16, np::bf16)
- `np::f16::from_f32(x)`, `from_f64`, `to_f32()`, `to_bits()`; `a.astype::<np::f16>()` (F16C bulk path from `f32`), `h.astype::<f32>()`
- 16-bit types are `Num` and `Float`: arithmetic and `exp`/`sin`/... compute in f32 and round once; `sum`/`mean`/`var`/`std` accumulate in f32
- `.npy` `<f2` read/write for f16; bf16 has no NumPy dtype (no `.npy`)
- `matmul` on f16 rounds every partial sum to 16 bits (NumPy accumulates in f32): cast to f32 first

## Advanced indexing (integer arrays)
- `a.slice(&np::s![[0, 2], [1, 3]])` is `a[[0, 2], [1, 3]]`; arrays may be literals, `Vec`s, `&Array<i64|i32|usize>` or a 1-d `&Array<bool>` mask; mix freely with ranges, ints and `np::NEW_AXIS`
- Index arrays broadcast; result is a copy; separated advanced axes move to the front (NumPy rule)
- `a.slice_assign(&np::s![[0, 2], [1, 3]], values)` assigns (last write wins)
- `np::ix_(&[&r, &c])`, `take_along_axis(&a, &idx, axis)`, `put_along_axis(&mut a, &idx, v, axis)`, `put(&mut a, ind, v)`, `choose(&sel, &[&c0, &c1])`, `ravel_multi_index(&[&r, &c], &dims)`, `unravel_index(&flat, &shape)`; index arrays are `Array<i64>`

## Masked arrays (np::ma)
- `np::ma::masked_array(data, Some(mask))` (`None` = nomask), `masked_where(&cond, a)`, `masked_invalid(&a)`, `masked_equal/greater/less/...(&a, v)`, `masked_inside/outside`, `masked_values`
- `np::ma::filled(&m, v)`, `compressed(&m)`, `getmask(&m)`, `getdata(&m)`, `count(&m)`; `m.count_axis(k)`, `m.get(&[i])` is `None` when masked
- Operators `&m + &n`, `&m / &n`, scalars and plain arrays mix in; masks propagate; division by zero and out-of-domain `sqrt`/`log` become masked
- Reductions skip masked values: `m.sum()` etc. return `Option<T>` (`None` if all masked); `sum_axis`, `mean_axis`, `std_axis`, `min_axis`, `argmax_axis` ... return a `MaskedArray`
- Display `[1.0 -- 3.0]`

## Discrete Fourier Transform (np::fft)
- `np::fft::fft(&a)`, `ifft(&a)` — FFT over last axis of a real or complex array, return `Array<Complex<F>>`
- `np::fft::rfft(&a)` — real FFT over last axis, `n/2 + 1` bins
- `np::fft::irfft(&z, None)` or `irfft(&z, Some(n))` — inverse real FFT, returns `Array<F>`
- `np::fft::fft2(&a)`, `ifft2(&a)` — 2-d FFT over last two axes
- `np::fft::fftfreq(n, d)`, `rfftfreq(n, d)` — sample frequencies
- `np::fft::fftshift(&a)`, `ifftshift(&a)` — shift zero-frequency to centre

## Polynomials (np::poly and np::polynomial)
- Legacy `np::poly`: coefficients 1-d, highest power first (`[1.0, -3.0, 2.0]` is `x^2 - 3x + 2`): `polyval`, `polyfit`, `polyadd`, `polysub`, `polymul`, `polydiv`, `polyder`, `polyint`, `roots`.
- Modern `np::polynomial`: classes `Polynomial`, `Chebyshev`, `Legendre`, `Laguerre`, `Hermite`, `HermiteE` with lowest-order first coefficients, domain/window mappings, operators `+ - * / % divmod pow`, `.eval(x)`, `.roots()`, `.deriv(m)`, `.integ(m, k, lbnd)`, `.fit(x, y, deg)`, `.convert()`, `.linspace(n)`.
- Submodules in `np::polynomial`: `chebyshev`, `legendre`, `laguerre`, `hermite`, `hermite_e`, `polynomial`, `polyutils` with `*val`, `*fit`, `*der`, `*int`, `*roots`, `*gauss`, `*vander`, `*weight`, `poly2*`, `*2poly`.

## Statistics, signal, sets and einsum (crate root)
- `np::cov(&m, bias, ddof)` — covariance matrix of rows. `np::corrcoef(&x)` — Pearson correlation
- `np::histogram(&a, bins, range, density, weights)` — returns (counts, edges). `np::histogram_bin_edges(&a, bins, range)`
- `np::bincount(&x, weights, minlength)` — counts of non-negative i64
- `np::digitize(&x, &bins, right)` — bin index for each element
- `np::average(&a, weights)`, `np::average_axis(&a, weights, axis)` — weighted average
- `np::quantile(&a, q)`, `np::quantile_axis(&a, q, axis)`
- `np::nanquantile(&a, q)`, `np::nanquantile_axis(&a, q, axis)`
- `np::convolve(&a, &v, mode)`, `np::correlate(&a, &v, mode)` — 1-d signal convolution/correlation (ConvolveMode)
- `np::diff(&a, n, axis)` — n-th discrete difference
- `np::gradient(&f, dx)` — returns Vec<Array<F>>. `np::gradient_axis(&f, spacing, axis, edge_order)`
- `np::interp(&x, &xp, &fp, left, right)` — 1-d linear interpolation
- `np::trapezoid(&y, spacing, axis)` — trapezoidal integration
- `np::cross(&a, &b)` — cross product. `np::kron(&a, &b)` — Kronecker product
- Sets: `np::intersect1d(&a, &b)`, `np::union1d(&a, &b)`, `np::setdiff1d(&a, &b)`, `np::setxor1d(&a, &b)`, `np::isin(&element, &test_elements)`
- `np::einsum(subscripts, &[&a, &b])` — Einstein summation (supports "ij,jk->ik", "ii", ellipsis "...", diagonals)

## Random (np::random)
- `let mut rng = np::random::Rng::seed(42);` or `Rng::from_entropy()`
- `rng.random(shape)` — [0, 1). `rng.uniform(lo, hi, shape)`
- `rng.normal(mean, std, shape)`, `rng.standard_normal(shape)`
- `rng.integers(lo, hi, shape)` — Array<i64>, hi exclusive
- `rng.choice(&a, n, replace)`, `rng.shuffle(&mut a)`, `rng.permutation(n)`, `rng.permuted(&a, axis)`
- `rng.binomial(n, p, shape)`, `rng.poisson(lam, shape)`, `rng.exponential(scale, shape)`, `rng.beta(a, b, shape)`, `rng.gamma(shape, scale, shape)`
- Distributions: standard_exponential, standard_gamma, standard_cauchy, standard_t, chisquare, noncentral_chisquare, f, noncentral_f, laplace, logistic, lognormal, gumbel, rayleigh, pareto, power, weibull, wald, triangular, vonmises, geometric, negative_binomial, hypergeometric, multivariate_hypergeometric, logseries, zipf, multinomial, dirichlet, multivariate_normal (method: cholesky, eigh, svd), bytes
- Same seed gives same numbers on every platform. Not NumPy's numbers.

## I/O (np::io)
- `np::io::save_npy(path, &a)?`, `np::io::load_npy::<T>(path)?` — NumPy .npy v1/v2. Wrong dtype gives Error::DType
- `np::io::savez(path, &[("a", &a)])?`, `np::io::savez_compressed(path, &[("a", &a)])?` — .npz archive
- `np::io::load_npz::<T>(path)?` — loads all members into Vec<(String, Array<T>)>
- `let f = np::io::NpzFile::open(path)?;` — lazy .npz reader: `f.keys()`, `f.get::<T>("a")?`
- `np::io::save_csv(path, &a, ',')?`, `np::io::load_csv::<T>(path, ',', skip_header)?`
- `np::io::to_npy_bytes(&a)`, `np::io::from_npy_bytes::<T>(&bytes)?`

## Printing
- `println!("{a}")` — NumPy layout: `[[1. 2.]\n [3. 4.]]`, bools `[ True False]`, 0-d as the bare value
- `println!("{a:?}")` — `array([[1., 2.], [3., 4.]], dtype=float64)`

## Not supported in v0.1
datetime/struct dtypes, memory-mapped files, string arrays. (Complex arrays are supported since v0.2; complex linalg is not.)

## Files
- README.md — overview and quick start
- docs/NUMPY_MAPPING.md — every NumPy call with its rustnum equivalent
- docs/API.md — binding API contract
- docs/ARCHITECTURE.md — internals and how to add a function
- rustnum/examples/ — quickstart, linear_regression, pca, kmeans, image_ops

## NaN-aware reductions (added after v0.1)
- `nanvar nanstd` (+ `_ddof(ddof)`, `_axis(axis)`, `_ddof_axis(axis, ddof)`), `nanmedian`, `nanmedian_axis(axis)`, `nanpercentile(q)`, `nanpercentile_axis(q, axis)` — floats
- `nanargmax nanargmin` (flat usize; all-NaN panics), `nanargmax_axis nanargmin_axis`; `nanprod nancumsum nancumprod` (+ `_axis`)

## Sorting, searching and conditional selection (added after v0.1)
- `np::lexsort(&[&k0,&k1], axis)` (last key primary), `np::flatnonzero(&a)`, `a.partition(kth, axis)`, `a.argpartition(kth, axis)`
- `np::select(&[&c..], &[&x..], default)`, `np::piecewise(&x, &[&c..], &[&f..])` (`&dyn Fn(T)->T`), `np::extract(&cond, &a)`
- `np::place(&mut a, &mask, &[v..])`, `np::copyto(&mut dst, src, Some(&mask))`, `np::trim_zeros(&a, "fb")`

## Index helpers (added after v0.1)
- `np::tril_indices(n, k, None)`, `triu_indices`, `tril_indices_from(&a, k)`, `triu_indices_from` -> `(rows, cols)`
- `np::diag_indices(n, ndim)`, `diag_indices_from(&a)`, `np::fill_diagonal(&mut a, val, wrap)`, `np::mask_indices(n, f, k)`
- `np::ndindex(&shape)`, `np::ndenumerate(&a)` — iterators

## Shape and creation extras (added after v0.1)
- `np::rot90(&m, k, (0, 1))`, `np::dstack(&[..])`, `np::column_stack(&[..])`, `np::row_stack(&[..])`, `np::atleast_1d/2d/3d(&a)`
- `np::geomspace(start, stop, num)`, `np::vander(&x, Some(n), false)`, `np::fromiter(iter, None)`, `np::frombuffer::<T>(&bytes, None, 0)`
- `np::around(&a, decimals)`, `np::real_if_close(&re, &im, tol)` (pair form), `a.is_posinf()`, `a.is_neginf()`

## Stride tricks (added after v0.1)
- `np::sliding_window_view(&x, &[w], None)` — zero-copy view; `np::as_strided(&x, &shape, &strides)` — element strides, bounds-checked

## Bit operations (added after v0.1)
- `np::bitwise_and/or/xor(&a, &b)`, `np::bitwise_not(&a)`, `np::invert(&a)`, `np::left_shift(&a, n)`, `np::right_shift(&a, n)`; operators `& | ^ ! << >>` on i32/i64/u8/usize arrays
- `np::packbits(&a, axis, "big")`, `np::unpackbits(&a, axis, count, "big")`, `np::bitwise_count(&a)`; trait `np::Integer`

## Functional helpers (added after v0.1)
- `np::vectorize(|x: f64| ..).call(a)` / `.call2(a, b)` / `.call3(a, b, c)` — scalar closure lifted over arrays with broadcasting
- `np::apply_along_axis(|lane| ..., axis, &a)`, `np::apply_over_axes(|a, axis| ..., &a, &[0, 2])`

## Text I/O (np::io) (added after v0.1)
- `np::io::loadtxt::<f64>(path, Some("#"), delimiter, skiprows, usecols, max_rows)?`, `np::io::savetxt(path, &x, fmt, delim, newline, header, footer, comments)?`
- `np::io::genfromtxt::<f64>(path, comments, delimiter, skip_header, skip_footer, filling, usecols, names, max_rows)?` -> `(array, names)`

## Print options (added after v0.1)
- `np::set_printoptions(np::PrintOptions { precision: 3, ..np::get_printoptions() })`, `np::get_printoptions()`, `let _g = np::printoptions(opts);` (scoped)

## Histograms, einsum_path, tensor inverse and solve (added after v0.1)
- `np::histogram2d(&x, &y, [Bins; 2], range, density, weights)` -> `(H, xedges, yedges)`; `np::histogramdd(&sample, &[Bins], range, density, weights)` -> `(H, edges)`
- `np::einsum_path("ij,jk->ik", &[&a, &b], "greedy")` -> `(path, report)`; `np::linalg::tensorinv(&a, ind)?`, `np::linalg::tensorsolve(&a, &b, axes)?`

## datetime64 / timedelta64 (v0.2)
- Units are types in `np::datetime`: `Y M W D h m s ms us ns`. `np::DateTime64<D>`, `np::TimeDelta64<D>` are array elements (`Array<np::DateTime64<D>>` is `datetime64[D]`)
- `DateTime64::<D>::parse("2024-03-05")?`, `::new(count)`, `.value()`, `.cast::<V>()`, `::NAT`, `np::isnat(&a)`, `np::datetime_as_string(&a)`
- `&a - &b` (td), `&a + &t`, `&t * 3`, `&t / &u` (f64), `t.floor_div(&u)`, `&t % &u`; `t.sum()/mean()/cumsum()`; same unit only, `astype::<DateTime64<s>>()` converts units; `NaT` sorts last
- `Array::<DateTime64<D>>::arange(start, stop, step)`; `.npy` `<M8[D]` / `<m8[s]` round trip with NumPy

## Structured dtypes (v0.2)
- `rustnum::record! { pub struct Point { x: f64, y: f64 } }` makes `Point` an array element (fields: numbers, complex, f16, datetimes, nested records)
- `a.field::<f64>("x")` -> `Array<f64>` (`a['x']`), `a.set_field("x", v)`, `a.argsort_order(&["x", "y"])`, `a.sort_order(&["x"])` (1-d, stable, unnamed fields break ties)
- `.npy`/`.npz` store the structured `descr` `[('x', '<f8'), ('y', '<f8')]`, readable by NumPy; `<Point as np::Record>::FIELDS` / `descr()`

## Python bindings (rustnum-py, v0.2)
- `rustnum-py/` is a PyO3 (`abi3-py39`) workspace crate, not a default member: `cargo build --release -p rustnum-py` or `maturin build --release`; `import rustnum_py as rn`
- `rn.ndarray` over float64/float32/int64/bool with NumPy-style creation, operators, indexing, reductions, `@`, `rn.linalg`, `rn.random`; `numpy.asarray(x)` is zero-copy via `__array_interface__`
